tools.name: get_store_policy
tools.description: A store's price adjustment and price match policy. For requests like "does Target do price matching?", "does John Lewis refund if the price drops?", "Currys price promise", "what's Best Buy's price adjustment policy?", "will Costco refund the difference?". With an item name it adds links to check to

tools.name: check_price_drop_claim
tools.description: Can I get the difference back? For requests like "I bought a TV at Best Buy 9 days ago for $499 and it's $449 now, can I get the difference?". Says whether a claim is likely (likely, likely_if_member, unlikely, check or no_drop), the amount, and the steps. With an item name it adds a Cheapest Price

tools.name: get_claim_reminder
tools.description: Calendar reminder for the last day to claim a price drop. Returns a calendar file (.ics) with an all-day event on the store's last claim day, how to claim and the policy link, with alerts 3 days before and on the day. Nothing is stored. check_price_drop_claim gives this link as add_to_calendar when

tools.name: list_stores
tools.description: Every store covered, plus card price protection. For requests like "which stores give you money back if the price drops?" or "does my credit card have price protection?". With country=GB, lists the UK policies.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_price_drop_claim · Private data: get_claim_reminder · Public sink: check_price_drop_claim · Destructive: check_price_drop_claim, get_claim_reminder.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_price_drop_claim · Private data: get_claim_reminder · Public sink: check_price_drop_claim · Destructive: check_price_drop_claim, get_claim_reminder

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
